[[File:Müller - Mathematical Treatise, 1760 - 1378597.jpg|thumb|''Mathematical Treatise'', 1760]]
'''John Muller''' (1699 – June 1784) was a [[mathematician]] and [[engineer]] from the [[Holy Roman Empire]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://thesaurus.cerl.org/record/cnp00580812/|title= Muller, John (1699 - 1784) in CERL Thesaurus}}</ref>

== Life ==
Born '''Johann Müller''' in the Holy Roman Empire, he moved to London in 1736.

In 1741 he was appointed deputy head of the [[Royal Military Academy, Woolwich]], where he performed all the teaching duties of [[Martin Folkes]].<ref name="ODNB">{{cite ODNB|id=19514|first=Steven A.|last=Walton|title=Muller, John}}</ref> He transformed the institution into a disciplined cadet academy with the help of [[Thomas Simpson]].<ref>{{cite book|url= https://books.google.com/books?id=nIKVQCeI1FUC|title= The Development of Newtonian Calculus in Britain, 1700-1800 by Niccolò Guicciardini|isbn= 9780521524841|last1= Guicciardini|first1= Niccol-|date= 13 November 2003}}</ref> In 1754 he became first master of the Academy, after Folkes's death.<ref name="ODNB"/> He was later appointed Professor of Artillery and Fortification (and "Preceptor of Engineering, etc. to his Royal Highness the Duke of Gloucester"); he retired in 1766. During his time at the Academy Muller carried out gunnery experiments with [[Thomas Desaguliers|Colonel Desaguliers]], described in the second edition of ''A Treatise of Artillery''.<ref>{{cite book | last1 = Muller | first1 = John | title = A Treatise of Artillery| edition = second| location = London | publisher = John Muller | date = 1768  | url = https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt/search?q1=desaguliers;id=nyp.33433009107370;view=1up;seq=9;start=1;sz=10;page=search;orient=0}}</ref>

Muller married Mary Horn on 29 December 1774, at St Martin-in-the-Fields, Westminster. He died at his home in Eaton Street (now Greet Street), London in June 1784.<ref>{{Citation | title = Died | newspaper = General Evening Post | location = London | date = 26–29 June 1784}}</ref> The contents of his library were auctioned at the Military Library, Whitehall early in 1785.<ref>{{Citation | title = This day is published a catalogue of books... | newspaper = Morning Post and Daily Advertiser | location = London | date = 22 January 1785}}</ref>
 
Muller’s works were concerned with mathematics and fortification. At the Academy there were strict instructions on which topics each instructor was to teach,<ref>{{cite book | last1 = Royal Military Academy, Woolwich | title = Rules and Orders for the Royal Military Academy at Woolwich | edition = Second | location = London | date = 1776  | url = http://find.galegroup.com/ecco/retrieve.do?sgHitCountType=None&sort=Author&tabID=T001&prodId=ECCO&resultListType=RESULT_LIST&searchId=R1&searchType=BasicSearchForm&currentPosition=1&qrySerId=Locale(en%2C%2C)%3AFQE%3D(0X%2CNone%2C45)Rules+%26+Orders+for+the+Royal+Military+Academy%3AAnd%3ALQE%3D(BA%2CNone%2C124)2NEF+Or+0LRH+Or+2NEK+Or+0LRL+Or+2NEI+Or+0LRI+Or+2NEJ+Or+0LRK+Or+2NEG+Or+0LRF+Or+2NEH+Or+0LRJ+Or+2NEM+Or+0LRN+Or+2NEL+Or+0LRM%24&retrieveFormat=MULTIPAGE_DOCUMENT&userGroupName=loughuni&inPS=true&contentSet=ECCOArticles&&docId=CW3308992859&retrieveFormat=MULTIPAGE_DOCUMENT&docLevel=FASCIMILE&workId=CW3308992859&relevancePageBatch=CW108992859&showLOI=&contentSet=&callistoContentSet=ECLL&docPage=article&hilite=y | access-date = 3 June 2019}}</ref> which included a list of works to be used; several of Muller's books were his included.

== Works ==
*A Mathematical Treatise: Containing a System of Conic-sections; with the doctrine of fluxions and fluents, applied to various subjects (1736)<ref>{{cite book | last1 = Muller | first1 = John | title = A Mathematical Treatise: Containing a System of Conic-sections; with the doctrine of fluxions and fluents, applied to various subjects  | location = London | publisher = John Muller | date = 1736  | url = https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=mdp.39015065258850;view=1up;seq=9 | access-date = 3 June 2019}}</ref>
*A Treatise Containing the Elementary Part of Fortification (1746)<ref>{{cite book | last1 = Muller | first1 = John | title = A Treatise Containing the Elementary Part of Fortification| location = London | publisher = John Muller | date = 1736  }}</ref>
*Elements of Mathematics (1748, also titled A System of Mathematics)
*A Treatise Containing the Practical Part of Fortification (1755)<ref>{{cite book | last1 = Muller | first1 = John | title = A Treatise Containing the Practical Part of Fortification | location = London | publisher = The Royal Academy of Artillery | date = 1755  | url = https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=mdp.39015022660024;view=1up;seq=9 | access-date = 3 June 2019}}</ref>
*A Treatise on Artillery (1757; later editions were titled A Treatise of Artillery)
*The Field Engineer; translated from the French (1759)
*Traité analytique des sections coniques, fluxions et fluentes. Avec un essai sur les quadratures, et un traité du mouvement (1760)<ref>{{cite book | last1 = Muller | first1 = John | title = Traité analytique des sections coniques, fluxions et fluentes. Avec un essai sur les quadratures, et un traité du mouvement.| location = London | publisher = The Royal Academy of Artillery | date = 1760  | url = https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_eWVyqon-dw0C/page/n4| access-date = 3 June 2019}}</ref>
*A New System of Mathematics (1769)
*New Elements of Mathematics: or, Euclid corrected (1773)<ref>{{cite book | last1 = Muller | first1 = John | title = New Elements of Mathematics: or, Euclid corrected | edition = Second | location = London | publisher = John Muller | date = 1773  | url = https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=mdp.39015063881273;view=1up;seq=5 | access-date = 3 June 2019}}</ref>
